what: Screenshot Beautifier turns a plain screenshot into a polished image ready for social media, presentations, documentation or a portfolio.

Place your screenshot on a gradient, solid colour or your own background image, with padding, rounded corners and a soft shadow. Add a simple browser window or phone frame drawn by the tool, tilt it slightly, add a small watermark, and choose a size made for Twitter/X, Instagram, LinkedIn or 16:9 slides. The PNG is exported at 2× by default so text stays crisp.
Everything is drawn in your browser, so private screenshots are never uploaded.
uses: Share app features on social media
Post a feature screenshot that stands out in a busy feed.
Give every screenshot in an announcement the same frame and background.
Present screenshots with consistent padding and shadow.
Show web and app designs inside clean browser or phone frames.
Make step-by-step screenshots easier to read with space around them and your handle as a watermark.
tutorial: Take a screenshot and press Ctrl+V (⌘+V on Mac) on the page, or drop or choose an image file. "Try with a sample" loads a demo screen.
Under "Background" choose Gradient and click a preset, or set two colours and the angle. You can also choose Solid colour, Your own image or Transparent.
Choose a "Frame": browser window (light or dark, with optional address bar text), title bar only, or phone. Set "Padding", "Corner rounding", "Shadow" and "Tilt".
Pick a "Canvas size" such as Twitter / X post, Instagram square, Instagram portrait, Story, LinkedIn post or 16:9, or Fit the screenshot.
Type your name or handle in "Watermark text" and choose its corner.
Click "Download PNG". The button shows the exact pixel size. In supported browsers you can also click "Copy image" and paste it straight into a post.
features: Ctrl+V or a Paste button, no saving to a file first.
Or solid colours, your own image, or transparency.
Generic browser window, title bar and phone frames, drawn crisply at any size.
Soft, medium or strong shadow that follows transparent edges.
Twitter/X, Instagram square and portrait, Story, LinkedIn and 16:9.
Or 1× for smaller files and 3× for extra detail.
Automatically light or dark to suit the background.

example.title: Worked example: a feature post for X
example.text: Dev took a 1440 × 900 px screenshot of a new dashboard. He pastes it with Ctrl+V, picks the purple-to-pink gradient, chooses Browser window (light) and types app.example.com in the address bar. He keeps padding at 10%, sets corner rounding to 3%, a medium shadow and a tilt of 0°, chooses Twitter / X post (16:9) and types @devmakes as the watermark. Download PNG gives a 2400 × 1350 px image with crisp text.

tips: Keep tilt small, 2 to 5 degrees, or none for text-heavy screens.
Crop your screenshot to the interesting part before adding it; less clutter looks better.
Use the dark browser frame with dark-mode screenshots, and the light one with light screens.
Choose Fit the screenshot for blog posts and docs, and a fixed size for social media so nothing is cropped by the platform.
Before sharing, check the screenshot for private details; use Blur & Censor Image first if needed.
problems: Make sure an image, not a file path, is on your clipboard: take the screenshot again and paste with Ctrl+V on the page. Some browsers block the Paste button; the keyboard shortcut still works.
Export at 2× or 3×, and start from a full-resolution screenshot rather than a scaled-down copy.
Your browser does not allow copying images. Use Download PNG instead.
The screenshot looks small on the canvas
Lower the Padding, or choose a canvas size closer to your screenshot's shape.
